plan.title: Connect a bot: Copy for <bot>, pending requests under Bots, connected notice
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: PAN-5069 (Part A, bot side; parent PRD)

narratives.Problem: Connecting a bot through the connector reach shows a pairing string plus four npx commands, an export and a config block; closing the dialog loses the code and Bots shows nothing pending; Grok Bot offers only Public MCP; nothing tells the operator when a bot pairs. PAN-5069 shipped the bot's one resumable command, so the dashboard side must now make it one paste and one approval.
narratives.Proposal: Replace the connector intent map with an in-memory connector request store (30-minute codes, derived live/expired/used state, 24 h retention), add root-only routes for waiting requests, cancel, notices and dismiss, and on the frontend add connectMessage (pure, deterministic), a 'Copy for <bot>' button that mints and copies one message with a clipboard fallback, a 'Waiting to connect' list under Bots with Copy again / Copy new / Cancel, Grok Bot's connector reach first, a non-blocking Needs-you notice with Revoke and Dismiss, and docs. Full detail: .pan/drafts/PAN-5070.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- A machine-side Approve/Deny card
- Phone push for the connected notice
- Persisting waiting requests or notices across a dashboard restart
- Changing pan mcp connector connect/login/pair/serve or their output (PAN-5069)
- The account activate page (PAN-5071)
- Integration READMEs, SKILL.md and Grok Bot mcp.json (PAN-5072)
- Removing the Tailscale, This computer or Public MCP reaches, or any botSnippets.ts export
- Changing browser, machine or phone pairing-code lifetimes (they stay 10 minutes)
- Adding route-scopes.ts rows for the new root-only routes
- Editing docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md

autoDecisions.summary: Cancel deletes the request and burns its code; no 'cancelled' status is stored
autoDecisions.rationale: Nothing reads a cancelled row; deleting is simpler and the burned code can no longer pair anything, so hasConnectorIntent answering false is safe.

autoDecisions.summary: A code consumed at the handshake or taken without a finished exchange lists as 'used' and offers Copy new, never Copy again
autoDecisions.rationale: takePairingById burns the code on any outcome; Copy again would hand the bot a dead code that fails with pairing-code-refused.

autoDecisions.summary: Waiting requests and notices are retained 24 h after expiry or pairing
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the issue's 24 h notice window and keeps every request at least as long as its code, so the cross-refusal guard never lapses early.

autoDecisions.summary: platform is optional in POST /api/connectors/pairing and defaults to 'other'
autoDecisions.rationale: Existing callers and tests post { name } only; the CLI's own default is 'other'.

autoDecisions.summary: The button reads 'Copy for <platform label>' (e.g. 'Copy for Grok Bot')
autoDecisions.rationale: The parent PRD's flow says 'pick the bot … click Copy for <bot>'; the platform is the bot the operator picked.

autoDecisions.summary: The manual pairing string and commands stay in the dialog under a collapsed 'Set up by hand instead'
autoDecisions.rationale: The parent PRD lists changing the manual login/pair/serve path as a non-goal; collapsing keeps it available without crowding the one-paste flow.

autoDecisions.summary: The connected notice is a non-blocking row in Needs-you's System group, shown only to root viewers
autoDecisions.rationale: No agent waits on it (PAN-5108 harness-update precedent) and its routes are root only, like MCP sign-ins.

autoDecisions.summary: No new frontend test files; tests extend botSnippets.test.ts and DecisionsPanel.test.tsx
autoDecisions.rationale: Both are already in scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt, and this keeps the plan within the 25-file finalize limit.
Its intent-store bullet stays accurate at its level and defers detail to docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md, which this plan updates; editing it would exceed the file budget.

items.title: Connector pairing codes live 30 minutes, with two non-consuming credential readers

narrative.Action: PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-5070.md W-1. Give issuePairingCredential an optional { ttlMs } (default PAIRING_CREDENTIAL_TTL_MS, prune unchanged); export pairingCredentialState(pairingId) -> 'live'|'expired'|'gone' (never consumes) and revokePairingById(pairingId) -> boolean; add CONNECTOR_PAIRING_TTL_MS = 30 * 60_000 in connector-pairing.ts and issue connector codes with it. routes/pairing.ts keeps calling issuePairingCredential() with no argument (10 minutes). Tests use vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] }).

items.title: Given fake Date, when issueConnectorPairing runs, then the returned expiresAt is exactly 30 minutes after the system time
Given fake Date, when issuePairingCredential() runs with no argument, then its expiresAt is exactly 10 minutes after the system time
pairingCredentialState returns 'live' for a fresh code, 'expired' 30 minutes + 1 ms later, and 'gone' after takePairingById consumes it
revokePairingById returns true once and false on a second call, and takePairingById then returns 'unknown'
Replace connector intents with an in-memory connector request store

expected_outputs: connector-pairing.test.ts passes, including the unchanged W-7 cross-refusal tests

narrative.Action: PRD W-2: implement the exact API listed there (issueConnectorPairing({ name, scopes, platform? }) (platform defaults to 'other') -> { requestId, pairingString, expiresAt }; takeConnectorIntent stamps takenAt and never deletes; markConnectorRequestPaired; hasConnectorIntent true for any stored request; listConnectorRequests with derived state live/expired/used and pairingString only when live; cancelConnectorRequest burns the code via revokePairingById and deletes; listConnectorNotices; dismissConnectorNotice; prune at expiresAt + 24 h (pending) and pairedAt + 24 h (paired)). Import CONNECT_PLATFORMS/ConnectPlatform from src/lib/mcp/connector/connect-output.ts. Rewrite the 'hands out an intent once' and 'refuses an expired intent…prunes it' tests as the PRD describes. Do not edit routes/connectors.ts; it keeps compiling because platform is optional.

items.title: Given an issued request, when takeConnectorIntent runs twice, then the first call returns { requestId, name, scopes }, the second returns null, and hasConnectorIntent still returns true
Given a taken-but-unpaired request or one whose code takePairingById consumed, listConnectorRequests reports state 'used' and omits pairingString
Given fake Date, an untaken request lists as 'expired' 30 minutes + 1 ms after issue, and at expiresAt + 24 h + 1 ms the next listConnectorRequests drops it and hasConnectorIntent returns false
cancelConnectorRequest burns the code (takePairingById returns 'unknown') and removes the row; a second cancel returns null
After markConnectorRequestPaired, listConnectorRequests no longer returns the request and listConnectorNotices returns it; after dismissConnectorNotice, listConnectorNotices no longer returns it
POST /api/connectors/pairing takes platform; the exchange marks the request paired

narrative.Action: PRD W-3. parsePairingBody returns { name, scopes, platform } (absent -> 'other'; not in CONNECT_PLATFORMS -> 400 'platform must be one of grok-bot, grok-build, hermes, openclaw, other'); handleConnectorPairing answers { requestId, pairingString, expiresAt } with no-store and logs platform and requestId but never the pairing string; handleConnectorsExchange calls markConnectorRequestPaired(intent.requestId, record.id) right after createAccessToken.

items.title: POST /api/connectors/pairing with platform 'grok-bot' returns 200 with a UUID v4 requestId, a parseable pairingString and Cache-Control no-store
POST /api/connectors/pairing with platform 'xai-api' returns 400 whose error lists grok-bot, grok-build, hermes, openclaw, other; a body without platform still returns 200
Given a successful connector exchange, listConnectorNotices() returns one notice whose connectorId equals the minted tokenId
Given an exchange that answers 409 link-key-in-use, listConnectorRequests() reports that request as state 'used'
GET /api/connectors lists waiting requests; DELETE /api/connectors/requests/:id cancels one

narrative.Action: PRD W-4. handleConnectorList answers { connectors, requests: listConnectorRequests() }. Add handleConnectorRequestCancel (root only, 404 'no pending connector request with id <id>', activity log with the name, no pairing string) and the DELETE /api/connectors/requests/:id route (rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest first) in connectorsRouteLayer. Add the no-loss row and update the GET /api/connectors row's door text exactly as the PRD gives them. Do not add route-scopes rows. The route-level test must pass the mutation gate with the internal token (write <OVERDECK_HOME>/internal-token, _resetInternalTokenCacheForTests(), send INTERNAL_TOKEN_HEADER and Content-Type: application/json, remoteAddress 127.0.0.1), as agent-requests-routes.test.ts does; an unauthenticated request gets the same rejection from both DELETE routes and proves nothing.

items.title: GET /api/connectors as the internal token returns requests with one entry of state 'live' carrying a pairingString for a freshly issued request
Cancelling a waiting request returns 200 { ok: true }, a second cancel returns 404 'no pending connector request with id …', and a device credential kind gets 403

Given the internal-token header, a DELETE /api/connectors/requests/<uuid> request driven through connectorsRouteLayer returns 404 with error 'no pending connector request with id <uuid>' (the cancel handler), never 'no connector with id'
tests/unit/lib/overdeck/no-loss-matrix.test.ts passes with a row whose surface is 'DELETE /api/connectors/requests/:id'
GET /api/connectors/notices and POST /api/connectors/requests/:id/dismiss

narrative.Action: PRD W-5. handleConnectorNotices (root only, rejectUnauthorizedDashboardRequest on the route) returns { notices } filtered to connectorIds in listActiveRecordsOfKind('connector'); handleConnectorNoticeDismiss (root only, rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest on the route) returns { ok: true } or 404 'no connector notice with id <id>'. Add both routes to connectorsRouteLayer and both no-loss rows. Route-level tests use the same internal-token setup as W-4.

items.title: After a successful exchange, GET /api/connectors/notices returns one notice with id, connectorId, name, scopes and pairedAt, and its JSON contains no 'overdeck-connector:' text
After handleConnectorRevoke removes that connector, GET /api/connectors/notices returns an empty notices array

POST /api/connectors/requests/<id>/dismiss returns 200 and the notice is gone; an unknown id returns 404 'no connector notice with id <id>' (also when driven through connectorsRouteLayer with the internal-token header); a device credential kind gets 403 on both routes

Given the internal-token header, GET /api/connectors/notices driven through connectorsRouteLayer returns 200 { notices: [] }, and no-loss-matrix.test.ts passes with rows for 'GET /api/connectors/notices' and 'POST /api/connectors/requests/:id/dismiss'
connectMessage: the one copy message, pure and deterministic

expected_outputs: botSnippets.test.ts passes including the new connectMessage describe block

narrative.Action: PRD W-6. Create connectMessage.ts with CONNECT_PLATFORM_IDS, ConnectPlatformId, CONNECT_PLATFORM_LABELS, connectPlatformFor, connectMessage (exact text in the PRD, shellQuote on pairing string and bot name), connectMessageFor (version serverVersion else 'latest'; machine label environment label, else parseConnectorPairLink(pairingString)?.machineLabel, else 'this machine') and writeClipboard (resolves false, never throws). Import only botSnippets.ts and @overdeck/contracts; never import botsApi.ts. Tests go in the existing botSnippets.test.ts (already in scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt).

items.title: connectMessage with version 0.61.0, bot name 'Grok Bot' and platform grok-bot returns text containing the line npx -y @overdeck/core@0.61.0 mcp connector connect '<pairing string>' --name 'Grok Bot' --platform grok-bot
A bot name Ed's bot renders in the command as 'Ed'\''s bot', and the output contains no 'token', 'export ' or 'mcp_servers' text
Calling connectMessage twice with the same inputs returns byte-identical strings; connectPlatformFor('xai-api') returns 'other' and every other BotPlatform maps to itself
connectMessageFor with no environment uses @overdeck/core@latest and the pairing string's n label; writeClipboard resolves false when navigator.clipboard is undefined
Grok Bot offers the Overdeck connector reach first

narrative.Action: PRD W-7. BOT_PLATFORMS grok-bot reaches become ['connector', 'public']; the dialog's Access-step condition becomes platform === 'grok-bot' && reach === 'public' (never reach === 'public' alone: the xAI API is public-only and needs its scope checkboxes for oauthLevelForScopes); connectorConfigFor returns null for grok-bot and the config CopyField renders only when non-null. Rewrite 'renders only the Public MCP reach for Grok Bot' and make the Grok Bot Public MCP tests click 'Public MCP' first. Keep every botSnippets.ts export.

items.title: Given the dialog, when the operator clicks Grok Bot, then the 'Overdeck connector' reach radio is checked and a 'Public MCP' radio is also rendered
With Grok Bot on the connector reach the Access step renders the scope checkboxes; with Grok Bot on Public MCP it renders the OAuth approval note instead
Given the xAI API platform (Public MCP), the Access step still renders the scope checkboxes and 'Show setup' with Operate ticked produces a token command containing '--level operate'
Given Grok Bot with Public MCP selected and Public MCP on, 'Show setup' renders a Grok Bot mcp.json containing the public URL
Bots API client: platform on pairing, cancel, notices, dismiss and the access label

Add ConnectorRequestRow, ConnectorNoticeRow, BOTS_CONNECTOR_NOTICES_QUERY_KEY, cancelConnectorRequest, dismissConnectorNotice, fetchConnectorNotices ([] on any failure or non-array body), connectorAccessLabel (decision 11), and an optional platform argument plus requestId result on createConnectorPairing. items.title: createConnectorPairing('bot', scopes, 'grok-bot') sends a POST body with platform 'grok-bot', and without the third argument the sent body contains no platform key
cancelConnectorRequest sends DELETE /api/connectors/requests/<encoded id> and dismissConnectorNotice sends POST /api/connectors/requests/<encoded id>/dismiss, both with the mutation headers

Copy for <bot>: one click mints the code and copies the message

narrative.Action: PRD W-9. Connector-reach button text is `Copy for ${platformEntry.label}`; handleCreate posts platform via connectPlatformFor, builds the message with connectMessageFor and the environment query, calls writeClipboard, and sets output { kind: 'connector', pairingString, expiresAt, message, copied }. ConnectBotOutput's connector branch renders the copied/fallback sentence, the expiry, a 'Message' CopyField, the 'waits under Settings → Anywhere → Bots' sentence, and a <details> 'Set up by hand instead' holding today's pairing string, commands and config, then Done.

items.title: Given the Hermes connector form, the submit button reads 'Copy for Hermes'; clicking it posts /api/connectors/pairing with platform 'hermes'

narrative.Action: PRD W-10. loadConnectors returns { connectors, requests } (requests [] when absent). BotsPanel renders 'Waiting to connect' rows (name; platform label · access label · expiry text), with Copy again for live, Copy new for expired/used (create with the row's name/scopes/platform, then cancel the old id, then copy), Cancel for every row (no confirm), invalidating BOTS_CONNECTORS_QUERY_KEY after each; success toast 'Copied — paste it into <label>.'; a failed copy shows a 'Message' CopyField under the row.
